candidates.label: about

candidates.label: safetyConsideration
candidates.comment: Any potential safety concerns, interactions, or adverse reactions associated with a dietary supplement. Also called supplement warnings, safety warnings, adverse effects. Examples: `St. John's Wort` safetyConsideration `"May interact with antidepressants"`, `Creatine Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Not recommended for individuals with kidney issues"`, `Vitamin D Supplement` safetyConsideration `"Avoid excessive dosage"`.

candidates.label: expertConsiderations
candidates.comment: An expert considerations relation between a diet and the medical expert advice pertinent to that dietary plan. Also called: medical advice, professional guidance, health warnings. Examples: "Keto Diet" expert considerations "Consult a doctor if you have kidney issues", "Vegan Diet" expert considerations "Ensure adequate B12 supplementation", "Low-Sodium Diet" expert considerations "Monitor blood pressure regularly".

candidates.label: risks
candidates.comment: The specific physiological dangers or adverse effects associated with a particular diet plan. Also called diet hazards, health risks of diet, diet side effects. Examples: `Keto Diet` risks `"Nutrient deficiencies"`, `Fad Diet` risks `"Metabolic imbalance"`, `Vegan Diet` risks `"Vitamin B12 deficiency if not supplemented"`.

candidates.label: warning
candidates.comment: A warning relation between a drug and any FDA or other safety advisories. Also called drug warning, safety advisory, health alert. Examples: "Drug warning 'May cause drowsiness.'", "Drug warning 'https://fda.gov/drug-warnings/xyz'", "Medication warning 'Do not exceed recommended dose.'".

candidates.label: negativeNotes
candidates.comment: Negative considerations or drawbacks associated with a product or described in a review. Also called cons, disadvantages, downsides, criticisms. Examples: "Product X negativeNotes 'short battery life'", "Review Y negativeNotes 'poor customer service'", "Software Z negativeNotes 'steep learning curve', 'frequent crashes'". Distinct from positiveNotes, which describes favorable aspects.

candidates.label: breastfeedingWarning
candidates.comment: Any precaution, guidance, or contraindication related to a drug's use by breastfeeding mothers. Also called: lactation warning, nursing caution, breastfeeding safety. Examples: "Drug 'Medication X' breastfeedingWarning 'Consult doctor before use'", "Drug 'Drug Y' breastfeedingWarning 'Not recommended for breastfeeding mothers'."

candidates.label: possibleComplication
candidates.comment: A medical attribute describing a potential unexpected and unfavorable evolution or outcome of a medical condition. Also called potential adverse event, risk, secondary condition, complication risk. Examples: Diabetes has a possible complication of 'kidney failure'. Surgery has a possible complication of 'infection'. A medical condition has a possible complication of 'worsening symptoms'.

candidates.label: accessibilityHazard

candidates.label: increasesRiskOf

candidates.label: parentItem
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a discussion item and its preceding item or a creative work it comments on. Also called part of, replies to, refers to, is a response to. Examples: A comment is a parent item of another comment. A question is a parent item of an answer. An answer is a parent item of a follow-up comment. Distinct from comment, which points from something to a comment about it.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: isPartOf
candidates.comment: A part-whole relation indicating that an item or creative work is a component of a larger creative work or resource. Also called component of, member of, contained in, element of. Examples: A chapter isPartOf 'a book'. An episode isPartOf 'a TV series'. A web page isPartOf 'a website'. Distinct from hasPart, which expresses the inverse relationship (the whole *has* a part).

candidates.label: subTrip
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger trip and a smaller trip that is a component or segment of it. Also called "trip segment", "part of trip", "daily itinerary", "trip leg". Examples: "The multi-day journey has subTrip Day 1", "The grand tour's subTrip is the visit to Rome", "This trip includes several subTrip components."

candidates.label: parentService
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a broadcast service and a broader broadcast service it is a variation or component of. Also called belongs to, is a variation of, is part of, is a channel of. Examples: BBC One Scotland is a parent service of BBC One. A regional news channel is a parent service of a national news channel. A specific sports channel is a parent service of a broader sports network.

candidates.label: superEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a smaller event and the larger event of which it is a part. Also called "part of larger event", "parent event", "contained within event", "main event". Examples: "The concert has superEvent the music festival", "The presentation's superEvent is the conference", "This workshop is part of a superEvent summit.". Distinct from subEvent, which points from the larger event to the smaller one.

candidates.label: itemListElement
candidates.comment: A list composition relation between an item list and its individual elements, which can be simple text, existing entities, or list items with additional context. Also called list components, list entries, elements of list, items in list. Examples: An item list has itemListElement 'First Item'. An item list has itemListElement 'Product A'. An item list has itemListElement a ListItem for 'Task 1'. Distinct from item, which refers to the entity *within* a ListItem, not the ListItem itself or a direct string/entity in the list.

candidates.label: hasPart

Examples: "A book has a part that is a chapter.", "A symphony has a part that is a movement.", "A website has a part that is a specific page.". Examples: "An organization has an offer catalog of its products.", "A service has an offer catalog of its packages.", "The person maintains an offer catalog."

candidates.label: hasOccupation
candidates.comment: An occupation relation between a person and their current occupation. Also called profession, job, employment. Examples: "A person has an occupation as a software engineer.", "She has an occupation as a doctor.", "His occupation is a teacher."

candidates.label: requiredQuantity
candidates.comment: A required quantity relation between a how-to item and the amount of that item needed. Also called quantity needed, amount required. Examples: "A how-to item 'sugar' has a required quantity '1 cup'.", "A crafting project needs a required quantity '5 sheets of paper'.", "A recipe step specifies a required quantity '2 eggs'."

candidates.label: inventoryLevel
candidates.comment: A stock quantity relation between a demand, offer, or product and its current approximate availability in inventory. Also called stock level, quantity in stock, available quantity, current stock. Examples: An offer has an inventoryLevel of '100 units'. A product has an inventoryLevel of 'low stock'. A demand has an inventoryLevel of '50 units available'.

candidates.label: amountOfThisGood
candidates.comment: An amount of this good relation between a type and quantity node and the numerical quantity of a specific good included in an offer. Also called quantity, number of items, item count. Examples: "A shopping cart item's amount of this good is '2'.", "The offer specifies an amount of this good as '5'."

candidates.label: hasMeasurement
candidates.comment: A measurement relation between a certification, offer, product, or size specification and a quantitative value representing a specific measurement. Also called item measurement, dimension, size value. Examples: "A product has a measurement for its height.", "An offer includes a measurement for package weight.", "The certification has a measurement of carbon footprint."

candidates.label: orderQuantity
candidates.comment: The number or quantity of a specific item ordered within an order item. Also called item quantity, ordered amount, number of units. Examples: "OrderItem A orderQuantity 2", "OrderItem B orderQuantity 5", "OrderItem C orderQuantity 1". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on total items for shipping.

candidates.label: amount
candidates.comment: An amount relation between a financial entity (e.g., loan, grant, money transfer) and the monetary value or number associated with it. Also called value, sum, quantity of money. Examples: "A loan's amount is '$10,000'.", "The grant's amount is '€5,000'.", "A money transfer's amount is '250'."

candidates.label: eligibleQuantity
candidates.comment: An eligible quantity relation between a demand, offer, or price specification and the quantitative value representing the ordering quantities for which it is valid. Also called "valid quantity range", "order quantity limit", "bulk discount quantity". Examples: "Offer 'Bulk Discount' eligibleQuantity 'Minimum 10 units'", "Price specification eligibleQuantity '5-100 items'", "Shipping charge eligibleQuantity 'Over 50 kg'".

candidates.label: offerCount
candidates.comment: The total number of individual offers aggregated for a product. Also called number of offers, offer quantity, total offers. Examples: "Product A AggregateOffer offerCount 10", "Service B AggregateOffer offerCount 5", "Item C AggregateOffer offerCount 20". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.

candidates.label: numItems
candidates.comment: A limit on the number of items being shipped for which specific shipping conditions apply. Also called item quantity limit, shipping item count, maximum items. Examples: "Free Shipping Conditions numItems 'max 5'", "Bulk Discount Shipping numItems 'min 10'", "Special Rate Shipping numItems '1-3'". Distinct from orderQuantity, which is the quantity of a specific item in an order.

candidates.label: numberOfBeds
candidates.comment: The quantity of a specific bed type available within a lodging unit. Also called bed count, quantity of beds, available beds. Examples: "King Bed Details numberOfBeds 1", "Twin Bed Details numberOfBeds 2", "Queen Bed Details numberOfBeds 1". Distinct from numberOfBedrooms, which specifies the number of rooms designated as bedrooms.

relations.definition: Shows that infrastructure development made an event possible
relations.embedding_query_text: enabled_by: Shows that infrastructure development made an event possible

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: data
candidates.comment: An association relation between an instantaneous event and the data linked to it. Also called: event data, associated data, event information. Examples: "Sensor Reading Event" data "temperature: 25C, humidity: 60%", "Log Entry Event" data "User 'admin' logged in from IP 192.168.1.1", "System Alert Event" data "Error code 500: Database connection failed".

candidates.label: broadcastOfEvent
candidates.comment: An event that is being broadcast by a broadcast event. Also called: televised event, event broadcast. Examples: "BroadcastEvent 'Super Bowl Live' broadcastOfEvent 'Super Bowl LVIII'", "BroadcastEvent 'Concert Stream' broadcastOfEvent 'Live Music Concert'."

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: subEvent
candidates.comment: A hierarchical relation between a larger event and a smaller event that is a component or part of it. Also called "part of event", "component event", "nested event", "event within event". Examples: "The conference has subEvent a keynote speech", "The festival's subEvent is a specific concert", "This event includes a subEvent workshop.". Distinct from superEvent, which points from the smaller event to the larger one.

candidates.label: eventStatus
candidates.comment: An event status relation between an event and its current status type. Also called "event condition", "status of event", "event state". Examples: "Event 'Concert' eventStatus 'EventCancelled'", "Event 'Meeting' eventStatus 'EventScheduled'", "Event 'Festival' eventStatus 'EventRescheduled'".

candidates.label: workFeatured
candidates.comment: A featured work relation between an event and a creative work, indicating that the work is highlighted or showcased within the event. Also called showcased work, highlighted work, exhibited work. Examples: ExhibitionEvent workFeatured PaintingA, FestivalEvent workFeatured SculptureB, ConferenceEvent workFeatured ResearchPaperC. Distinct from workPerformed, which is a live rendition of a work, and workPresented, which is a specific presentation of a movie at a screening event.

relations.definition: Links an official statement to a specific achievement or outcome
relations.embedding_query_text: attributes_success: Links an official statement to a specific achievement or outcome

instances: Kim Beom-ho's Statement -> Incheon Becomes World's Busiest Airport

candidates.label: result
candidates.comment: The outcome or product generated by an action. Also called outcome, product, output, consequence. Examples: `WriteAction` result `Book`, `CookAction` result `Meal`, `CreateAction` result `Artwork`. Distinct from `resultComment` and `resultReview` which are specific types of results.

candidates.label: prescribingInfo
candidates.comment: A linking attribute providing a URL to the official prescribing information for a drug. Also called drug information link, medication guide, prescribing details. Examples: A drug has prescribing info at 'https://example.com/drug-info/xyz'. The medication provides prescribing info via a URL. The pharmaceutical company offers prescribing info on its website.

candidates.label: resultComment
candidates.comment: The specific comment created or sent as the outcome of a comment or reply action. Also called generated comment, comment outcome, produced comment. Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: resultReview
candidates.comment: The specific review created as the outcome of a review action. Also called generated review, review outcome, produced review. Examples: `ReviewAction on Product` resultReview `Customer's Product Review`, `ReviewAction on Movie` resultReview `Critic's Movie Review`, `ReviewAction on Service` resultReview `User Service Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: linkRelationship
candidates.comment: A link relationship type relation between a link role and its descriptive text. Also called: hyperlink relation, link type, relationship attribute. Examples: "LinkRole linkRelationship 'nofollow'", "LinkRole linkRelationship 'alternate'", "LinkRole linkRelationship 'canonical'".

candidates.label: characterAttribute
candidates.comment: An attribute relation describing a particular aspect of a fictional character within a game or video game series. Also called "character trait", "character property", "game attribute". Examples: "Video game character attribute 'Strength'", "RPG game character attribute 'Magic Resistance'".

candidates.label: winner
candidates.comment: A winner relation between a losing action and the person who won it. Also called victor, triumphant participant, successful party. Examples: ChessMatchLoseAction winner Alice, RaceLoseAction winner Bob, CompetitionLoseAction winner Charlie.

candidates.label: positiveNotes
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute providing positive considerations, highlights, or pros for a product or an item being reviewed. Also called pros, advantages, benefits, highlights. Examples: A product has positive notes like 'Excellent battery life'. A review has positive notes like 'User-friendly interface'. The service has positive notes like 'Responsive customer support'. Distinct from negativeNotes, which provides negative considerations.

candidates.label: educationalCredentialAwarded
candidates.comment: An educational credential awarded relation between a course or program and the credential received upon successful completion. Also called "award received", "qualification granted", "certificate earned". Examples: "Course 'Introduction to Python' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Certificate of Completion'", "Program 'MBA' educationalCredentialAwarded 'Master of Business Administration'", "Training 'First Aid' educationalCredentialAwarded 'First Aid Certification'".

candidates.label: contentRating
candidates.comment: An official classification relation for a creative work, indicating its content rating. Also called "age rating", "maturity rating", "content advisory". Examples: "Movie contentRating 'PG-13'", "Video game contentRating 'ESRB Teen'".

relations.definition: Indicates the number of international destinations an airport connects to
relations.embedding_query_text: serves: Indicates the number of international destinations an airport connects to

candidates.label: departureAirport
candidates.comment: A geographical origin relation between a flight and the airport from which it originates. Also called: origin airport, departure airfield, flight departure point. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure airport "London Heathrow Airport", "Flight UA123" departure airport "San Francisco International Airport". Distinct from arrivalAirport, which is the destination airport.

candidates.label: arrivalAirport
candidates.comment: An arrival airport relation between a flight and the airport where it concludes. Also called destination airport, landing airport, final airport. Examples: "A flight's arrival airport is 'LAX'.", "The flight's arrival airport is 'Heathrow Airport'."

candidates.label: flightNumber
candidates.comment: A flight number relation between a flight and its unique identifier, typically including the airline IATA code. Also called: flight ID, airline code, flight identifier. Examples: "Flight from London to New York" flight number "BA177", "Flight from Tokyo to San Francisco" flight number "UA838", "Flight from Sydney to Dubai" flight number "EK413".

candidates.label: passengerSequenceNumber
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the sequence number assigned to a passenger for a flight reservation by the airline. Also called boarding sequence, passenger number, flight sequence. Examples: A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number '001'. A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number 'A12'. A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number '34B'.

candidates.label: icaoCode
candidates.comment: An ICAO code relation between an airport and its ICAO identifier. Also called ICAO identifier, airport ICAO code, international airport code. Examples: "An airport has an ICAO code 'KJFK'.", "The airport is identified by its ICAO code.", "This airport uses an ICAO code.". Distinct from iataCode, which is a different type of airport identifier.

candidates.label: departureTerminal
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a flight and its departure terminal identifier. Also called: terminal number, flight terminal, departure building. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure terminal "Terminal 5", "Flight UA123" departure terminal "Terminal 3". Distinct from arrivalTerminal, which is the arrival terminal.

candidates.label: arrivalTerminal
candidates.comment: A terminal identifier for a flight's arrival location. Also called: flight destination terminal, terminal of arrival. Examples: "Flight BA286 arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 5'", "Flight from Tokyo arrivalTerminal 'North Terminal'", "Flight to JFK arrivalTerminal 'Terminal 4'". Distinct from arrivalStation, which is for train trips.

candidates.label: areaServed
candidates.comment: An area served relation between a contact point, offer, organization, or service and the geographic region where it is available. Also called service area, coverage region, delivery zone. Examples: "A restaurant's area served is 'Downtown'.", "The delivery service's area served is 'California'.", "An organization's area served is 'Worldwide'."

candidates.label: departureGate
candidates.comment: An identification relation between a flight and its departure gate identifier. Also called: gate number, boarding gate, flight gate. Examples: "Flight BA249" departure gate "Gate A12", "Flight UA123" departure gate "Gate 34B". Distinct from arrivalGate, which is the arrival gate.

candidates.label: iataCode
candidates.comment: An IATA code relation between an airline or airport and its IATA identifier. Also called IATA identifier, airline code, airport code. Examples: "An airline has an IATA code 'AA'.", "An airport has an IATA code 'JFK'.", "This entity is identified by its IATA code."

candidates.label: applicationStartDate
candidates.comment: An application start date relation between an educational or occupational program and the date when it begins accepting applications for an enrollment cycle. Also called application opening date, submission start date. Examples: "A university program's application start date is '2022-09-01'.", "The scholarship program's application start date is 'January 1st'."

candidates.label: opens
candidates.comment: The specific time a place or service opens on a given day or days of the week. Also called opening time, start of business, daily opening hour. Examples: "Monday OpeningHoursSpecification opens '09:00'", "Weekend OpeningHoursSpecification opens '10:00'", "Weekday OpeningHoursSpecification opens '08:30'". Distinct from closes, which specifies the closing time.

candidates.label: datePosted
candidates.comment: A temporal publication relation between a CDCPMD record, job posting, real estate listing, or special announcement and its online publication date. Also called: posting date, publication date, listing date. Examples: "Job Opening" date posted "2023-10-25", "Apartment for Rent" date posted "2023-10-20", "Public Health Alert" date posted "2023-03-01T09:00:00Z". Distinct from datePublished, which is a more general property for first publication.

candidates.label: validFrom
candidates.comment: A valid from relation between a certification, demand, financial incentive, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, opening hours specification, permit, or price specification and the date it becomes valid. Also called effective date, start date, activation date. Examples: "Offer validFrom '2023-11-01'", "Permit validFrom '2023-01-01T09:00:00'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validFrom '2024-01-01'". Distinct from validThrough or validUntil, which specify the end of validity.

candidates.label: validThrough
candidates.comment: A valid through relation between a demand, financial incentive, job posting, location feature specification, monetary amount, offer, or opening hours specification and the date after which it is no longer valid. Also called expiration date, end date, valid until. Examples: "Offer validThrough '2023-12-31'", "JobPosting validThrough '2023-11-30'", "OpeningHoursSpecification validThrough '2024-12-31'". Distinct from validFrom, which specifies the start of validity. Distinct from validUntil, which is similar but for Permit only.

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

candidates.label: closes
candidates.comment: A temporal specification for opening hours, indicating the closing time for a place or service on a given day. Also called "closing time", "end of hours", "closes at". Examples: "Store opening hours closes '18:00'", "Service opening hours closes '22:30'". Distinct from opens, which specifies the opening time.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: releaseDate
candidates.comment: A release date relation between a product and the date it was made available to the public. Also called launch date, availability date, publication date. Examples: "A new smartphone model has a release date of 2024-03-01.", "A software update has a release date of 2023-11-15.", "A new car model has a release date of 2025-01-01.". Distinct from productionDate, which is when the item was manufactured.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: answerCount
candidates.comment: An answer count relation between a question and the total number of answers it has received. Also called number of responses, reply count, solution count. Examples: "A forum question's answer count is '5'.", "The quiz question's answer count is '10'."

candidates.label: numberOfItems
candidates.comment: The total number of items contained within an item list. Also called item count, list size, total items. Examples: "Shopping Cart ItemList numberOfItems 5", "To-Do List numberOfItems 10", "Search Results List numberOfItems 100". Distinct from numItems (for ShippingConditions), which is a limit on items for shipping.

candidates.label: numChildren
candidates.comment: The number of children included in a lodging reservation. Also called child count, number of kids, child guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numChildren 1", "Vacation Rental numChildren 3", "Family Suite Reservation numChildren 2". Distinct from numAdults, which specifies the number of adults.

candidates.label: toLocation
candidates.comment: A destination location relation between an action (like exercise, insert, move, or transfer) and the final place of the object or agent after the action. Also called destination, final location, arrival place. Examples: "MoveAction toLocation 'New York'", "TransferAction toLocation 'Warehouse B'", "ExerciseAction toLocation 'gym'". Distinct from location, which is the general place where something is or occurs.

candidates.label: numAdults
candidates.comment: The number of adults included in a lodging reservation. Also called adult count, number of grown-ups, adult guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numAdults 2", "Vacation Rental numAdults 4", "Single Room Reservation numAdults 1". Distinct from numChildren, which specifies the number of children.

candidates.label: itinerary
candidates.comment: A travel plan relation between a trip and the sequence of places or an item list detailing the destinations. Also called travel route, trip plan, destinations, journey path. Examples: A trip has an itinerary of 'Paris, Rome, London'. A trip has an itinerary of an ItemList detailing stops. A vacation package has an itinerary of 'Hawaii'.

candidates.label: target
candidates.comment: A destination relation between an action and its intended entry point or URL. Also called "action destination", "target URL", "entry point for action", "leads to". Examples: "The search action has target a search results page", "The button's target is a specific URL", "This action points to a target entry point."

candidates.label: repeatCount
candidates.comment: A repeat count relation between a schedule and the total number of times a recurring event will occur. Also called number of repetitions, event occurrences. Examples: "A weekly meeting schedule has a repeat count of 10.", "A training course schedule has a repeat count of 5.", "A daily alarm schedule has a repeat count of 365."

candidates.label: interactionCount
candidates.comment: A deprecated property indicating the number of user interactions with an item. Also called user interactions, engagement count, activity count. Examples: (No active examples for deprecated properties).

candidates.label: includesAttraction
candidates.comment: An attraction inclusion relation between a tourist destination and a tourist attraction located within it. Also called contains attraction, destination attraction, features attraction. Examples: "A tourist destination includes an attraction like a museum.", "The city includes an attraction for historical sites.", "This destination features a famous includes attraction."

candidates.label: position
candidates.comment: An ordinal attribute indicating the sequential position of an item within a series or list. Also called order, rank, sequence number, index. Examples: A list item has a position of '1'. A chapter in a book has a position of 'Chapter 3'. A search result has a position of '5'.

candidates.label: ratingCount
candidates.comment: A rating count relation between an aggregate rating and the total number of individual ratings contributing to it. Also called number of ratings, total ratings. Examples: "An aggregate rating has a rating count of 150.", "A product review summary has a rating count of 500.", "A movie's average rating has a rating count of 10,000."

candidates.label: taxonRank
candidates.comment: A classification of a taxon by its taxonomic rank, often expressed as a URI from a controlled vocabulary. Also called "taxonomic level", "rank in taxonomy", "biological classification". Examples: "The taxon has taxonRank 'Family'", "The species' taxonRank is 'Species'", "This taxon is classified by taxonRank 'Genus'."

candidates.label: bestRating
candidates.comment: A number or text representing the highest value allowed in a rating system. Also called: maximum rating, top score, highest possible rating. Examples: "Rating 'Product Review' bestRating '5'", "Rating 'Movie Score' bestRating '10'". Distinct from worstRating, which is the lowest value.

candidates.label: ratingValue
candidates.comment: A rating value relation between a rating and its numerical or textual score. Also called score, rating score, value of rating. Examples: "A movie review has a rating value of 4.5.", "A product has a rating value of 'Excellent'.", "A restaurant has a rating value of 3 stars."

candidates.label: reviewCount
candidates.comment: The total number of individual reviews contributing to an aggregate rating. Also called total reviews, number of reviews, review tally. Examples: `Product Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `150`, `Movie Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `5000`, `Service Aggregate Rating` reviewCount `75`.

candidates.label: starRating
candidates.comment: An official quality rating for a food establishment or lodging business, typically from a standards body. Also called "official rating", "quality rating", "hotel stars", "restaurant rating". Examples: "The hotel has starRating 5 stars", "The restaurant's starRating is 3 Michelin stars", "This lodging business received a 4-star rating.". Distinct from aggregateRating, which is a summary of user-generated reviews.

candidates.label: worstRating
candidates.comment: A worst rating relation between a rating and a number or text, specifying the lowest possible value within that rating system. Also called minimum rating, lowest score, bottom value. Examples: RatingSystem worstRating 1, ReviewRating worstRating "Terrible", StarRating worstRating 0. Distinct from bestRating, which specifies the highest possible value.

candidates.label: isTierOf
candidates.comment: A membership hierarchy relation between a member program tier and the larger member program it belongs to. Also called tier within, part of program, level of program. Examples: A 'Gold' tier isTierOf 'Loyalty Program X'. A 'Premium' tier isTierOf 'Subscription Service Y'. A 'Bronze' tier isTierOf 'Rewards Program Z'.

candidates.label: hasTierRequirement
candidates.comment: A tier requirement relation between a member program tier and a condition for joining that tier. Also called tier eligibility, membership condition, joining requirement. Examples: "A member program tier has a tier requirement of a specific credit card.", "The tier has a tier requirement of a minimum spend.", "This tier requires a tier requirement of an annual fee."
